correctness.rationale: Checked the literal all-agent every-good EFX quantifiers. For each leaf i, its envy of center is blocked iff X_i>=Y_i-1{sum_{j!=i}Y_j=0}; center envy of leaves requires S+1>=max_i X_i. Distinct labelled orientations induce independent binomial X_i and give the stated exact sum. When m>3R+2, center-to-dominant-leaf comparison forces Y_1>R, yielding B=intersection_{i>=2}{X_i>=ceil(r_i/2)}, central binomial slice H_m(Y) and an exact single odd-m exception (Y=0,X_1=(m-1)/2). Under each subsidiary r_i→infinity and fixed k, P(B)→2^{-(k-1)}, Y/R→1/2 in probability, so standardized central window tends to Phi(gamma/2)-1/2 or 1/2; local central binomial estimate and R→infinity yields the sharp small-R equivalent. Independently checked direct all-bundle deletion versus reduced conditions over selected multistars up to four goods per spoke; this finite check does not prove the CLT.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge novelty survives direct full-text comparisons: existence of a fair multistar orientation, exact counts for equal-spoke multistars, and EFX0 counts on simple bicliques do not determine the probability that a random orientation is fair when one spoke diverges and the subsidiary aggregate scales as sqrt(m). The exact weighted formula plus sharp Gaussian and subcritical windows are new motivated counting information; unindexed direct count remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: Other independent unindexed counts of random multistar orientations might contain equivalent binomial probability or CLT.
EFX convention varies across literature; zero-valued deletion is essential and comparisons must not conflate with EFX excluding zero goods.
